newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh hopes to tide over bank crisis.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh hopes to tide over bank crisis.

text.p: Bangladesh hopes to overcome the crisis in the banking system, triggered by huge bad loans, by injecting millions of dollars to beef up market liquidity, central bank officials said on Friday.
They said the government would give 16 billion taka ($368 million) to the fund-starved banks.

"I don't think the country's banking system will collapse due to the liquidity crisis. The government is taking all steps to overcome the weakness of the sector," Syed Amirul Mulk, a Finance Ministry secretary, said on Friday.
Central Bank governor Lutfar Rahman Sarkar said on Tuesday that the country's banking system was on the "verge of collapse".

Sarkar estimated the amount of outstanding bank loans at 130 billion taka ($3 billion) and said the country did not have adequate laws to deal with defaulters. "The defaulters are taking the advantage of legal loopholes," he said.
Mulk said the central bank had already identified seven commercial banks that were in bad shape due to the liquidity crisis.
"The central bank will take all possible measures to protect the interest of the depositors," he said.
Mulk declined to identify the seven commercial banks immediately, saying he did not want to cause new alarm among depositors.
Central bank officials said they hoped a substantial amount of bad loans could still come back to the lenders.
They said the $368 million would be injected immediately but declined to elaborate.
